messages:
Lena: Quick sync: after yesterday's adapter-inlined-admission flip, we saw multiple adapters start heavy KV warmups simultaneously for the same tenant. 
Diego: Seen those traces too. Two things: (1) adapters optimistically ACCEPT without coordination, (2) warmup is heavyweight and non-idempotent today.
Priya: We need a cheap coordination primitive that avoids an RPC on every enqueue. Ideas?
Lena: My rough idea: 3-tier path. Fast optimistic accept (no RPC). If the adapter intends to do heavy work it must attempt a lightweight RegisterClaim which is a O(1) in-memory op on scheduler leader for that shard.
Diego: What does RegisterClaim return?
Lena: {status: OK | CONFLICT | DEFER, claim_id?, ttl_ms?}. OK means you are owner and may start warmup. CONFLICT means someone else already owns it. DEFER indicates scheduler is overloaded; adapter should back off.
Omar: How do we ensure RegisterClaim itself doesn't become the hotspot? We shard registries and keep them leader-local. Also use consistent hashing on tenant id so RegisterClaim for the same tenant hits the same shard.
Jules: TTLs are important. Warmup must extend claim TTL with heartbeat calls. If heartbeat loops stop, scheduler can release claim.
Priya: Who extends TTL? Adapter sends periodic ExtendClaim(claim_id, progress). That also lets scheduler track warmup progress percent and decide preemption fairness.
Lena: We should also define semantics for fast optimistic accepts. If two adapters both fast-accept and both attempt to RegisterClaim concurrently, one will get OK, the other gets CONFLICT and should cancel its warmup. That requires warmup cancellation hooks in adapter.
Diego: Cancelling warmup mid-flight is tricky. Warmup should be cancellable but must make best-effort cleanup, and be safe to resume later (idempotent batches or idempotent reads). We'll document that warmup may re-run a prefix and must tolerate duplicate reads.
Priya: For low-op latency, RegisterClaim should be a tiny RPC (GRPC unary) returning a small payload. We can compress the path by returning a single byte status if possible. Avoid heavy proto envelopes.
Omar: For bursts where many adapters attempt RegisterClaim for many tenants, we need admission smoothing: scheduler returns DEFER and an approximate Retry-After ms; adapters do exponential backoff with jitter and maintain a local retry budget to avoid synchronized storms.
Jules: Metrics we should surface immediately: claim_attempts, claim_conflicts, claim_deferred, claim_ttl_extends, warmup_cancels, warmup_restarts. Gate rollout on claim_conflicts and increased client 503 rates.
Lena: Compatibility: make RegisterClaim optional. Old schedulers will ignore the field and adapter will fall back to previous optimistic-only behavior. Handshake at startup advertises registry version.
Diego: One more optimization: for very small warmups (eg < 50 keys), allow a "best-effort local warmup" without RegisterClaim; mark these as cheap in metrics so we can tune threshold.
Priya: Let's define API surface minimal set: RegisterClaim(tenant_id, host_epoch, expected_work_units) -> {status, claim_id?, ttl_ms?, retry_after_ms?}; ExtendClaim(claim_id, progress)-> {ok|not_found}; ReleaseClaim(claim_id)->{ok}; Heartbeat(claim_id)->{ok}.
Omar: Edge-case: leader failover while claim exists. Make claim epoch-bound (claim includes: shard_epoch, claim_seq). On leader failover, claims are invalidated and adapters should re-register. Scheduler will return not_found on ExtendClaim so adapter restarts process.
Jules: Integration test suggestions: simulate two adapters racing RegisterClaim, simulate leader failover during warmup, simulate DEFER flooding and ensure adapters backoff.
infra-bot: deploy-batcher v2.3 rolling to staging now. Build: https://ci.internal/release/4320001234
Lena: Action list: Diego/Omar design proto + sharded in-memory registry, Priya/Jules implement adapter fastpath + cancelable warmup, Ill write integration tests for races and leader failover. I'll open a draft RFC and link tests.
Diego: Also add a small doc section in ops-runbook about claim preemption and how to interpret the metrics.
Priya: Will include a small migration plan: start with optional registry in staging, watch claim_conflicts < 0.1% and client 5xx stable, then flip default on.
Lena: PR incoming in ~2d. Thanks all.
